question:
A plane monochromatic electromagnetic wave propagates through a **non-magnetic dielectric medium** (so $\mu=\mu_0$) of dielectric constant $K$.

At a point in the medium, the electric field is measured as
\[\vec E(x,t)=E_0\cos(\omega t-kx)\,\hat{j}.\]
A student claims:

"The relation $B_0=\dfrac{E_0}{c}$ is always true because $c$ is universal, so the magnetic field amplitude does not change in a dielectric."

Evaluate the claim and identify the correct magnetic field $\vec B(x,t)$, the wave speed $v$ in the medium, and the direction of energy flow.

Which option is correct?

options.B: $\vec B(x,t)=\dfrac{E_0}{c}\cos(\omega t-kx)\,\hat{k},\; v=\dfrac{c}{\sqrt{K}},\;$ energy flows along $+x$
options.D: $\vec B(x,t)=\dfrac{E_0}{c}\cos(\omega t-kx)\,\hat{j},\; v=c,\;$ energy flows along $+x$
